title: Decoding Echo Chambers: LLM-Powered Simulations Revealing Polarization in Social Networks

key_points.claim: Proposes an LLM-based agent simulation of a social opinion network to evaluate and counter polarization/echo chambers; motivated by limits of numeric/formula opinion models that ignore text.
key_points.evidence_quote: we propose an LLM-based simulation for the social opinion network to evaluate and counter polarization phenomena

key_points.claim: Network structure: three typical network topologies are built to represent different social interaction characteristics.
key_points.evidence_quote: We first construct three typical network structures to simulate different characteristics of social interactions.

key_points.claim: Agent behavior: agents interact via recommendation algorithms and update strategies through LLM reasoning.
key_points.evidence_quote: agents interact based on recommendation algorithms and update their strategies through reasoning and analysis

key_points.claim: Validation: compared against classic Bounded Confidence and Friedkin-Johnsen models and echo-chamber indices; reproduces polarization and echo chambers.
key_points.evidence_quote: By comparing these interactions with the classic Bounded Confidence Model (BCM), the Friedkin-Johnsen (FJ) model, and using echo chamber-related indices

key_points.claim: Intervention: two mitigation methods, active and passive nudges, reduce echo chambers in language-based simulations.
key_points.evidence_quote: We propose two mitigation methods—active and passive nudges—that can help reduce echo chambers

reliability_notes: Abstract only (abstract and metadata; full text PDF not fetched). Peer-reviewed COLING 2025 paper. No quantitative results available from the abstract.
